object_title_english: Egyptian crocodile mummy with mummified crocodile hatchlings on its back
classification_basis: description in Anderson & Antoine 2019 (wrappings removed before arrival; resin coated; textile fragments on snout and right side); fig. 1 not inspected by me
species_if_given: Crocodylus niloticus (adult Nile crocodile, per authors)
provenance: Kom Ombo (de Morgan excavation 1893; exact context undetermined)
acquisition: Presented by the Egyptian Government (Antiquities Service, J. de Morgan) 1895, via E.A.W. Budge
date_period: 14C on skin UBA-29791: 2518±27 BP, 792-542 cal BC (2 sigma)
description: Largest mummy in BM; over 25 mummified hatchlings (200-300 mm) individually wrapped, tied to Typha reeds on back; mouth tied; partly eviscerated, torso packed with textile; gastroliths; bovine forelimb bones in stomach (CT at Royal Veterinary College). Resin = conifer tar/pitch + beeswax.
bibliography: Anderson & Antoine 2019 (Creatures of Earth, Water, and Sky pp. 31-37, fig. 1-5); Budge 1904 Guide to the Third and Fourth Egyptian Rooms p. 66; De Cupere et al. 2023 PLOS ONE (cites 14C); exhibition 'Scanning Sobek' 2015-16
source_of_identification: Anderson, J. & Antoine, D. 2019. Scanning Sobek: Mummy of the Crocodile God, in Porcier, Ikram & Pasquali (eds), Creatures of Earth, Water, and Sky, Sidestone, pp. 31-32 fig. 1 (https://www.sidestone.com/openaccess/9789088907722.pdf)
notes: Composite: adult crocodile + >25 hatchlings on back. Likely also in BM collection online (uk_south agent).

classification_basis: description and photo/3D rendering in Berruyer et al. 2020 (completely unwrapped; few remaining textile parts; head and body broken apart; distal tail tip missing)
species_if_given: crocodile (Crocodylus sp.; not specified in extracted text)
